correctness.rationale: The published Gaussian normalization and Eqs. (7)–(8) match. The source uses depleted-first phenotype labels, so its LH, not its HL, is the same phenotype as the frozen record's explicitly replete-first HL (high under replete perception, low under depleted). In the frozen labels the log-ratio advantages against LL, HH, and LH are −pk, −ωk, and −k; the payoff gap is bounded below by min(T−R,P−S), and the probabilities have positive lower bounds for fixed finite noise, uniform also for σ≥1. This gives exponential fixation in the stated interior. The Gaussian derivative is σ^−2 times Cov(V,1_{V<c}), strictly negative; decreasing density at n=0 and increasing density at n=1 give ω(0)>c>ω(1). In resource logit coordinates the transient vanishes exponentially and the limiting drift is uniformly strictly inward outside each fixed neighborhood of the root. This yields finite entry and trapping, avoiding a spurious boundary limit from the n(1−n) factor. Expanding the two Gaussian integrals with uniform differentiated remainders gives ω−c=c(1−c)((1+c)/3−n)/(2σ²)+O(σ^−4); differentiation at the root gives the asserted negative resource eigenvalue in the triangular linearization. For k=−1 and D=0 the transient in the logit equation is exactly d/dt of b=(ε/c)log((1−x)/y), at every noise level. At infinite noise this yields the precise memory shift (ε/c)log(y_0/(1−x_0)). For equal initial marginals 1/2, b(0)=0 and b(t) decays uniformly exponentially for σ≥1. On stretched time subtract b from the logit; its slow drift differs from the limiting Lipschitz logit drift by O(σ^−2)+O(exp(−γσ²τ)), of integrated size O(σ^−2) on fixed compact intervals. Gronwall gives the cubic crossover for positive stretched times. Finite-physical-time continuous dependence gives the other iterated limit. The limits differ when n_0 differs from (1+c)/3, as in the stated example.
residual_risks: Only strictly interior initial conditions for the global claim; the exact memory and crossover use the specified payoff slice and linkage condition. Positive slow-time convergence does not imply uniform convergence through the fast layer at τ=0.

originality.rationale: The model, dominant action choices, interior stationary equation, phase regions and critical balance are prior; the review credits the quantified singular Gaussian critical-line result. The primary paper explicitly states squeezing toward the critical balance and has the post-fixation scalar equation, but its inspected equations, Fig. 4 and §III.3 do not resolve the finite-noise selected limit at the balance, the relaxation coefficient, or the full-dynamics initial-memory and crossover laws. Global convergence uses the old dominance and scalar signs, so it is not by itself the basis of the pass. The distinguishing result is the quantitative resolution of the singularity including the two protocols and uniform-away-from-zero slow limit.
residual_risks: The comparison is bounded to the inspected primary sections and accessible indexed statements. An unindexed derivative or equivalent formulation of the high-noise expansion and crossover could alter priority.

value.rationale: The balance is forced by the meeting of two previously identified phase boundaries, not a numerically chosen slice. Although the large-noise kernel expansion is elementary, the result resolves what the singular phase picture cannot: a universal finite-noise-selected resource, an explicit slow rate, and a different terminal state if complete noise is taken first, with a crossover law linking the two. This is a usable quantitative refinement of the model, not a new claim about the underlying game or a calibrated ecological timescale.
residual_risks: No finite-population interpretation or universal payoff-independent memory law is implied.
